chain: In Favor of the Light (Dun Morogh)

summary: Branstock Khalder sends a young priest from Coldridge Valley through the mountain pass to Kharanos for further study. There, Priest Trainer Maxan Anvol prepares the novice for greater duties and a chance to earn their first formal vestments.

sections.title: Leaving the Anvil
sections.body: You leave Anvilmar after showing dedication and understanding of Holy magic. Branstock Khalder sends promising novices beyond the mountains, where priests meet Dun Morogh’s needs and help defend its people.

sections.title: A Step Toward Kharanos
sections.body: The Coldridge Pass tunnel opens into central Dun Morogh, where Priest Trainer Maxan Anvol guides you beyond basic prayers. He teaches that service to the Holy Light calls for moral character, physical hardiness, and an unyielding will. Prove your resolve under his guidance, and you may receive your first formal garments of office.

faq.q: Who sends you on this journey?
faq.answer: Branstock Khalder, the priest trainer at Anvilmar in Coldridge Valley, sends you to Kharanos for further study after you show aptitude with the Holy Light.
Maxan Anvol is the priest trainer in the mountain village of Kharanos. He guides developing priests and teaches them to unite devotion with physical endurance and mental fortitude.

faq.q: What happens after reaching Maxan Anvol?
aliases: what follows in favor of the light
faq.answer: Maxan Anvol asks you to prove your worth by helping injured locals in Garments of the Light. Afterward, he awards you your first official priest robes.

faq.q: Why must priests leave Coldridge Valley so early?
faq.answer: Coldridge Valley teaches the basics of combat and spellcraft. In Kharanos, priests meet the needs and dangers of a wider community and learn to serve its people.

faq.q: Do human priests receive this same quest?
aliases: human in favor of the light
faq.answer: Human priests in Elwynn Forest undertake the same rite under the same name. Priestess Anetta in Northshire sends them to Priestess Josetta in Goldshire.

faq.q: How does the dwarven view of the Light differ here?
faq.answer: Dwarves value physical strength, will, and practical endurance alongside piety. Maxan Anvol teaches that serving the Light in freezing mountain peaks calls for strength of body as well as faith.

angles.text: As a priest, you leave basic training for active service and receive your first vestments.
As a dwarf, you join spiritual devotion with practical resilience as you leave Coldridge for Dun Morogh’s freezing winds.
